newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Motors to make up strike losses.
newsitem.headline: Kia Motors to make up strike losses.

text.p: Kia Motors Corp, South Korea's second largest carmaker, said on Thursday it would make up for losses suffered in almost four weeks of strikes with weekend production.
"The company and the labour union agreed to work weekends normally from this week to recover strike losses," said Kia spokesman Chun Sang-keun.
Chun said the strikes, which started in protest against passage of a controversial labour law on December 26 and continued until January 18, cost Kia about 320 billion won in lost production.
Normally, Kia workers take holidays on Sundays and on every other Saturday.
Kia earlier said its sales target for 1997 was set at 8.4 trillion won, compared with an estimated 6.6 trillion won in 1996.
